Hi Vanessa / Karthik,

Thanks for sending the MSA and order form. Our legal team attached a set of redlines — the high level asks are: 1) governing law to be California (our headquarters), 2) jurisdiction for disputes to be California state courts (no arbitration), and 3) a carveout for emergency equitable relief to remain with state courts.

We understand Redwood prefers arbitration and a Delaware choice of law; however the procurement team needs state-court jurisdiction for contract disputes to meet our internal policy.

Fwding Atlas redlines. Julie is asking for CA law + state court jurisdiction; they explicitly say no arbitration.

Quick thoughts: commercial team wants to keep arbitration (for predictability) and prefer Delaware as governing law for consistency across enterprise deals.

Proposed negotiation stance (commercial):
- Offer California governing law instead of Delaware (concession),
- Retain arbitration (mutual, JAMS or AAA) for monetary disputes,
- Explicit carveout: either party can seek temporary injunctive or other equitable relief in state courts (California) to preserve IP / emergency relief — Redwood keeps the right to seek urgent relief in courts.

Can legal draft short fallback language we can propose to Atlas? If we can present a single redline that keeps arbitration but preserves immediate injunctive relief in CA courts I think procurement might accept. If they push on courts-only, we may need to escalate.

—Vanessa

Vanessa / Karthik —

Thanks for the heads-up and attaching Atlas's redlines. Below is a draft negotiating position legal can support if commercial is comfortable with the concession on governing law.

Recommended compromise language (to propose to Atlas):
1) Governing Law: "This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of California, without regard to conflict of laws principles."

2) Dispute Resolution: "Except as set forth in the paragraph below regarding emergency equitable relief, any dispute, claim or controversy arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall be resolved by binding arbitration administered by JAMS in San Francisco, California, under the JAMS Comprehensive Arbitration Rules & Procedures. Judgment on the award rendered by the arbitrator(s) may be entered in any court having jurisdiction."

3) Equitable Relief Carveout: "Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party may seek temporary, preliminary or permanent injunctive relief or other emergency equitable relief in any state or federal court located in California, and the parties agree that such courts shall have exclusive jurisdiction over such requests for equitable relief."

Rationale:
- Governing law concession buys good will and is low legal risk.
- Arbitration keeps a predictable forum for commercial claims and avoids protracted multi-jurisdiction litigation.
- The carveout preserves ability to get immediate court-ordered injunctive relief in CA for IP/confidentiality issues.

If procurement insists on courts-only, ask for an escalation call with Atlas legal + our legal lead (Jordan) to discuss why arbitration is important (speed, confidentiality, enforceability on awards). If they force courts-only, we may need pricing/term concessions.

I can produce a redline with the three clauses above and a short memo for Vanessa to send to Atlas.

—Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Vanessa / Marissa,

Appreciate the quick reply and the compromise language. I ran this by our GC. Two notes from Atlas legal: 1) our GC is uncomfortable with arbitration as the primary forum — they want a courts-first approach for all contract disputes (not just equitable relief), and 2) they are open to a carveout for emergency injunctive relief, but want it explicitly spelled out that courts in California "retain sole and exclusive jurisdiction over injunctive relief."

If Redwood is firm on arbitration, Atlas is likely to push back on other commercial terms (pricing and support SLAs). Can we schedule a 30-minute call between Jordan (your legal lead), our GC (Mark), and procurement to try to bridge? Availability: Tue Jun 22 after 10am PT or Wed Jun 23 all day.

Thanks,
